Vice-President Kashim Shettima has assured Edo State of continued federal support in roads, healthcare, energy, agriculture, entrepreneurship and security, as the All Progressives Congress kicked off its presidential campaign in the state. Shettima spoke at the presidential rally, which also coincided with the second anniversary celebration of the Governor Monday Okpebholo administration, held at the Samuel Ogbemudia Stadium in Benin City. Shettima said the Federal Government would keep to its understanding with the Edo people, which is that no serious effort to close Nigeria’s infrastructure gap could succeed without the state. “We have come to assure you that you can count on us too. When we came to you four years ago, we said we could not address our nation’s infrastructure deficit without carrying Edo State along. We have not abandoned that agreement. “We are here to assure Edo people of continued federal support in roads, healthcare, energy, agriculture, entrepreneurship and security,” he said. He said work had started on the dualisation of roads to Ekpoma, Auchi and Okpella, as well as the Benin-Agbor-Sapele road, adding that the Federal Government was determined to build more roads in the state. The Vice President also spoke of federal support for Edo in healthcare, energy, entrepreneurship, agriculture and security. He pointed to ongoing efforts to secure the return of Benin artefacts and the transfer of ownership of the Benin treasures to Nigeria. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. According to him, Tinubu holds the governor in high regard and has backed him to serve the people of Edo. Okpebholo, in his remarks, pledged that Edo would deliver for the President in the January 2027 political contest, citing what he described as Tinubu’s contributions to the state. “In Edo State, we are ready to deliver come January 2027. The President has done so much for Edo people,” the governor said, adding that, “Today, we don’t owe salaries. We don’t owe pensioners. Construction work is going on everywhere.” He said the visible construction across the state was proof of his administration’s commitment to development and the welfare of workers. Former Edo State governor and senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, congratulated Okpebholo on two years in office and commended his efforts towards the development of the state. The President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, and the Chairman of the Progressive Governors’ Forum and Governor of Imo State, Hope Uzodimma, also encouraged residents to support the party, noting that the federal government would continue to support the state. Shettima had earlier sought the prayer, counsel, and goodwill of the Oba of Benin, Ewuare II, when he led members of the APC Presidential Campaign Council to the place. “I have always found Your Majesty’s personal journeys particularly instructive. Before the ascension of the throne, you represented Nigeria as a diplomat in several nations. “As we approach another democratic season, we seek Your Majesty’s prayer, counsel and goodwill. We value the role of the Benin throne, a promoter of peace, reconciliation and mutual respect. “Your Majesty understands that what ultimately matters is the welfare of the people and stability of the nation. We welcome your guidance and remain deeply ready to listen to the concerns of your Kingdom,” he stated. The Vice President described the Oba of Benin, whose wisdom and disposition he noted are deeply admired, as one of the torchbearers of African culture and civilisation. He also congratulated the paramount traditional ruler on the cordial relationship that exists between the federal and Edo State governments. “The Federal Government values the role of the Benin throne as a promoter of peace, reconciliation and mutual respect,” Shettima added. He highlighted notable accomplishments the Benin Kingdom has recorded from pre-colonial to contemporary times, including the repatriation of looted artefacts that have started finding their way back to the palace through the Oba’s efforts, calling it a matter of justice and national pride. Shettima noted that although the 1897 invasion of the Benin palace by British forces remained a painful chapter and a failed attempt to extinguish the dignity of the Benin people, the monarchy stands as a testament to their resilience through its art, craft, and civilisation—reminding everyone that progress and tradition enrich each other. In response, the Oba of Benin expressed delight over the visit, particularly acknowledging the role of Nigeria’s Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musa Musawa. “We will be praying for the nation. Most of them all the President. Everything is all said and done,” the monarch said. Accompanying the Vice President on the visit were Senate President Akpabio; Governors Okpebholo (Edo), Sheriff Oborevwori (Delta), and Uzodimma (Imo); Edo State Deputy Governor Dennis Idahosa; Oshiomhole; Pastor Osagie Ize-Iyamu; and other dignitaries. Adeyinka Adedipe
